### 💡 Intuition & Approach
Deduplicate visits per user and day, use the gaps-and-islands `ROW_NUMBER()` date offset trick to group consecutive dates, and rank streaks by length descending and earliest start date.

### ⚡ Implementation
```sql
WITH days AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT user_id, substr(visit_date, 1, 10) AS visit_day
  FROM visits
), islands AS (
  SELECT user_id, visit_day,
         CAST(julianday(visit_day) AS INTEGER) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY visit_day) AS grp
  FROM days
), streaks AS (
  SELECT user_id, MIN(visit_day) AS streak_start, MAX(visit_day) AS streak_end,
         COUNT(*) AS streak_length
  FROM islands
  GROUP BY user_id, grp
), ranked AS (
  SELECT user_id, streak_start, streak_end, streak_length,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
           PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY streak_length DESC, streak_start ASC
         ) AS rn
  FROM streaks
)
SELECT user_id, streak_start, streak_end, streak_length
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY user_id;
```

### ⏱️ Complexity Analysis
- **Time Complexity**: $\mathcal{O}(N \log N)$
- **Space Complexity**: $\mathcal{O}(N)$
